issues.description: Method: SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery. The problem statement (UML and textual description) declares acceptSupplyDelivery to take four parameters: (String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). However, both the provided template example call in Main and the solution implementation define/use a three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity). This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether to implement a 4-parameter method (including a supplier name) or the 3-parameter method used in code examples and the reference solution, potentially causing compilation or test mismatches depending on which signature is used.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across all artifacts. Recommended fix A (simpler): update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to specify the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and remove references to a supplier parameter. Ensure the UML method line and explanatory text reflect this 3-parameter form. Update any example calls in the problem statement to match. Alternative fix B: change the template Main and the solution SealSaloon to implement and call acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update all examples and UML accordingly. Choose one option and apply it everywhere so students see a single, unambiguous parameter list.

issues.description: The concept is the acceptSupplyDelivery method for registering a supply delivery. In the problem statement (UML and text) it is specified as acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) — i.e., a four-parameter method including a supplier name. In the template usage (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) the call is shop.acceptSupplyDelivery("Bacon", 50, 100); — a three-argument call. In the reference solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java) the implemented method is public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) — also three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This inconsistent API (four-parameter signature in the problem statement vs. three-parameter usage/implementation in template & solution) will confuse students: they may implement or attempt to call a four-parameter method as described in the spec, but the provided code examples and solution expect three parameters (or vice versa), preventing a clear mapping from requirement to code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the acceptSupplyDelivery API across all artifacts. Recommended fix: update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to require the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and remove the supplierName parameter from the spec, since both the template example and the provided solution use a three-parameter method. Alternatively, if the supplier name is required pedagogically, update the template Main and the solution implementation to use and implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update all calls accordingly. Ensure the chosen signature is used identically in the UML, textual description, template code examples, and reference solution.
